meta.title: AI paid media tools
meta.description: A maintained index of paid-media and measurement tools with MCP servers, agent plugins, CLIs, APIs and SDKs.
meta.scope: Tools that can materially support planning, buying, measuring, modelling, moving data, automating work or producing paid-media creative.

tools.name: Google Ads
tools.summary: Queries account structure and performance through Google Ads Query Language. The current official MCP surface is read-only.

developer.label: Google Ads API and client libraries

tools.access: Developer token, Google Cloud project and account credentials.
tools.caution: The MCP can inspect but cannot create or change campaigns. API access levels still apply.

tools.name: Meta Ads
tools.summary: Meta's hosted Ads AI Connector brings campaign data and actions into compatible assistants through MCP.
tools.access: Open beta; account and regional availability may vary.
tools.caution: Inspect the authenticated tool list and permissions before allowing campaign changes.

tools.name: TikTok for Business
tools.summary: A vendor-hosted MCP for campaign management, reporting, audiences and creative operations, with full and progressive-disclosure endpoints.
tools.access: TikTok for Business account and OAuth permissions.
tools.caution: The broad endpoint exposes hundreds of tools. Progressive disclosure is safer for smaller agent contexts.

tools.name: Microsoft Advertising
tools.summary: Microsoft's governed MCP connects compatible assistants to Microsoft Advertising API capabilities.
tools.access: Microsoft Advertising account and API permissions.
tools.caution: Confirm the live tool list and write scope after authentication.

tools.name: Amazon Ads
tools.summary: An official MCP layer over Amazon Ads API functionality, including multi-step tools for campaign creation, reporting and market expansion.
tools.access: Open beta for Amazon Ads partners with active API credentials.
tools.caution: The MCP can create, update and delete campaigns. Use review and approval controls before execution.

tools.name: Snapchat Ads
tools.summary: A hosted Ads MCP for retrieving Snapchat campaign data and insights from supported AI clients.
tools.access: Allowlist rollout and authenticated ad-account access.
tools.caution: The documented MCP is read-only even though the underlying Marketing API has broader capabilities.

tools.name: LinkedIn Ads
tools.summary: LinkedIn's Marketing APIs cover campaign management and reporting. We found community MCP wrappers, but no vendor-backed MCP source.
tools.access: Developer application, product approval and tier-specific permissions.
tools.caution: Do not treat a community wrapper as LinkedIn-supported. Marketing API access is gated by product and tier.

tools.name: Pinterest Ads
tools.summary: Pinterest's Ads API supports programmatic campaign and reporting workflows. No vendor-backed MCP source was verified.
tools.access: Pinterest developer application and authorised ad accounts.
tools.caution: Use the API directly or an integration layer, and identify the maintainer of any MCP wrapper.

tools.name: Reddit Ads
tools.summary: Reddit's Ads API v3 exposes campaign and account operations. No vendor-backed MCP source was verified.
tools.access: OAuth application and approved advertising access.
tools.caution: Community connectors should be checked against the current v3 API and Reddit's access terms.

tools.name: X Ads
tools.summary: The X Ads API exposes advertiser resources and reporting, while X's xurl CLI can make authenticated requests and ships with an official agent skill.
tools.access: Developer account and Ads API access; some endpoints require allowlisting.
tools.caution: X also operates a general X API MCP, but its published tool list does not establish Ads API coverage. Do not label it an Ads MCP without endpoint-level proof.

tools.name: Display & Video 360
tools.summary: Google's DV360 API can manage advertisers, campaigns, insertion orders, line items, targeting, creatives and users. Reporting uses a separate Bid Manager API.
tools.access: A Google Cloud project, OAuth 2.0 and a DV360 user with access to the relevant partner or advertiser.
tools.caution: The API can retrieve, create and update resources, but it does not return performance data and does not support every YouTube & Partners write workflow.

tools.name: Campaign Manager 360
tools.summary: The Campaign Manager 360 API supports large-scale trafficking, creative, conversion, reporting and attribution workflows.
tools.access: A Campaign Manager 360 account with API access, a permitted user profile, a Google Cloud project and OAuth 2.0 credentials.
tools.caution: Many resources are writable. User-profile permissions in Campaign Manager 360 govern what the API can change.

tools.name: Search Ads 360
tools.summary: The Search Ads 360 Reporting API provides high-volume, query-based reporting over campaigns, ads, keywords and performance data.
tools.access: OAuth 2.0 application credentials and access to the relevant Search Ads 360 manager or client account.
tools.caution: The reporting API is read-only. Offline conversion uploads use a separate Search Ads 360 API surface.

tools.name: Apple Ads
tools.summary: Apple's Platform API lets advertisers and agencies manage campaigns, ad groups and keywords, pull reports and work with App Store and Apple Maps ads.
tools.access: An Apple Ads API user with an eligible role and OAuth 2.0 credentials; third-party providers require separate registration.
tools.caution: API roles can be read-only or read-write. Verify the assigned role before using an automation layer.

tools.name: The Trade Desk
tools.summary: The Trade Desk's Open Agentic Kit provides MCP-based access to Ask Koa for platform data and actions, including campaign creation and monitoring.

plugin.label: No separate official agent plugin verified

tools.access: OAK is available to selected partners in private beta through their account representative. API credentials are also account-managed.
tools.caution: Published scope includes both data and actions. Treat campaign creation and other platform mutations as approval-gated operations.

tools.name: Google Analytics
tools.summary: Google's open-source MCP lets agents query Analytics reporting and administration data without changing the property.

cli.label: Package launcher only; no analytics CLI

tools.access: Google Cloud credentials and property permissions.
tools.caution: Read-only means the MCP cannot edit events, audiences or property settings.

tools.name: Google Tag Manager
tools.summary: The Tag Manager API can manage accounts, containers, workspaces, tags and triggers. No vendor-backed MCP source was verified.
tools.access: Google Cloud OAuth credentials and container permissions.
tools.caution: Publishing a container is a production change. Put review, environments and rollback around any agent workflow.

tools.name: Amplitude
tools.summary: Amplitude's hosted MCP can work with charts, dashboards, experiments, cohorts and taxonomy. It does not ingest event data.
tools.access: Amplitude account, project access and user-scoped permissions.
tools.caution: Write tools can change analytical assets and taxonomy. Event ingestion remains outside the MCP.

tools.name: Mixpanel
tools.summary: Mixpanel's vendor-hosted MCP brings product and behavioural analytics into compatible assistants.
tools.access: Mixpanel account and compatible MCP client.
tools.caution: The public announcement does not define a durable write boundary. Inspect the authenticated tools before use.

tools.name: Supermetrics
tools.summary: A marketing-data MCP that queries Supermetrics sources through one connection, alongside an API and an alpha command-line client.
tools.access: A valid subscription with Supermetrics API access.
tools.caution: The CLI is alpha. Source entitlements and query costs still depend on the subscription.

tools.name: DataForSEO
tools.summary: The official server and CLI browse DataForSEO documentation and make authenticated API requests for SERP, keyword, backlink and market data.

cli.label: Official CLI in the MCP package

tools.access: OAuth for hosted HTTP or API credentials for CLI and local stdio.
tools.caution: This supplies research data; it does not control paid-media accounts. API modules are billed and enabled separately.

tools.name: Airbyte
tools.summary: Airbyte exposes an agent MCP for working with connected data and a separate knowledge MCP for product documentation.

plugin.label: No separate official agent plugin verified

tools.access: Airbyte account or instance, configured sources and destinations.
tools.caution: Do not confuse the documentation-search MCP with the agent MCP that can act on connected data.

tools.name: Fivetran
tools.summary: Fivetran's Agent Context MCP exposes governed data context; its Connector SDK adds a CLI and official coding-agent integrations.
tools.access: Fivetran Context Layer for MCP; account permissions for API and SDK workflows.
tools.caution: The MCP is a context and retrieval surface, not a substitute for connector operations or warehouse access controls.

tools.name: Google MCP Toolbox for Databases
tools.summary: Google's open-source MCP toolbox connects agents to BigQuery and other databases through explicitly configured tools.
tools.access: Self-hosted configuration plus database credentials and permissions.
tools.caution: This is a general database layer, not a paid-media connector. Read/write risk depends entirely on the configured tools and database role.

tools.name: Snowflake
tools.summary: Snowflake's managed MCP lets agents reach governed Snowflake capabilities without deploying a separate server.
tools.access: Snowflake account, Cortex Agent configuration and role permissions.
tools.caution: Warehouse permissions remain the real control plane. Scope roles and exposed tools narrowly.

tools.name: Meridian
tools.summary: Google's open-source marketing mix modelling framework for estimating incremental impact and informing budget allocation.

cli.label: Python package, not a dedicated CLI

tools.access: Open source; requires model-ready historical data and Python expertise.
tools.caution: A model library is not an autonomous media optimiser. Inputs, priors, validation and decision rules remain practitioner work.

tools.name: Robyn
tools.summary: Meta's open-source marketing mix modelling package for estimating channel contribution and budget scenarios.

cli.label: R and Python package, not a dedicated CLI

tools.access: Open source; requires prepared data and statistical modelling expertise.
tools.caution: Robyn produces model outputs, not campaign changes. Treat automated budget recommendations as hypotheses requiring review.

tools.name: PyMC-Marketing
tools.summary: An open-source Bayesian marketing analytics package covering marketing mix modelling and customer-lifetime-value work.

cli.label: Python package, not a dedicated CLI

tools.access: Open source; requires Python and Bayesian modelling expertise.
tools.caution: The package supports analysis. It does not provide a governed connection to advertising accounts.

tools.name: Zapier
tools.summary: Zapier MCP lets assistants call scoped actions across Zapier's app catalogue; the Platform CLI is for building Zapier integrations.

plugin.label: MCP tool bundles, not a separate plugin

tools.access: Zapier account and connected apps; each successful MCP call consumes tasks.
tools.caution: A broad action catalogue can create real external changes. Keep servers client-specific and tools narrowly scoped.

tools.name: Pipedream
tools.summary: Pipedream provides hosted MCP servers across thousands of APIs, managed authentication, an SDK and a full `pd` CLI.

plugin.label: No separate official agent plugin verified

tools.access: Pipedream account; connected-app credentials are managed by Pipedream.
tools.caution: Tools inherit the permissions of connected accounts. Review annotations and separate development from production.

tools.name: n8n
tools.summary: n8n can expose an instance or a single workflow through MCP, and can also consume external MCP tools inside workflows.

plugin.label: Native nodes and skills, not a separate plugin

tools.access: n8n instance; enable MCP per instance and workflow, with user-scoped access.
tools.caution: Connected clients may share the same enabled workflow set. Workflow execution can trigger credentials and external writes.

tools.name: Figma
tools.summary: Figma's remote MCP can retrieve design context and, for supported clients and seats, create or modify native canvas content.

cli.label: No dedicated official Figma CLI verified

tools.access: Supported MCP client and Figma permissions; a Full seat is required for write-to-canvas.
tools.caution: Dev seats support read-oriented context. Canvas writes require both a Full seat and edit permission.

tools.name: Canva
tools.summary: Canva's remote MCP supports design creation and editing, assets, brand resources, search, export and collaboration.

plugin.label: AI Connector uses MCP; no separate plugin counted

tools.access: A Canva account and individual OAuth authorisation; app-development features have separate requirements.
tools.caution: The Apps CLI builds Canva apps. It is not a general command-line interface for day-to-day creative production.
